text.p: French carmaker Renault said it sold 1,785,520 vehicles worldwide in 1996, up from 1,745,346 the previous year.
In western Europe, its sales totalled 1,475,453 vehicles, up from 1,439,686, but its market share slipped to 10.4 percent from 10.8 percent, Renault said in a statement.

It sold 1,290,307 cars in western Europe, up from 1,241,478, but its market share slipped to 10.1 percent from 10.3 percent. Renault's car market share fell in Spain, Italy, France, the Benelux countries, Portugal, Austria and Switzerland last year, but rose in Germany and Britain.
In France, its car sales rose to 567,012 units last year, up from 563,712 in 1995, but its market share fell to 26.6 percent from 29.2 percent.

Sales director Patrick Faure said the group saw big swings in its market share in France last year -- it had 27.57 percent in the first quarter, fell to a low of 24.61 percent in the second quarter, then recovered to gain 26.83 percent in the third quarter and 27.09 percent in the fourth quarter.
He said the group was hurt by the transition between ageing and replacement models in the first half, and he said it failed to realise in time the extent of the price war waged in France.
"We tried for too long to be virtuous (in maintaining price levels), and that cost us sales," he told a news conference.

He said there was some good news although 1996 was a difficult year. The Clio and Megane were the best selling French cars in Europe, capturing 2.9 percent and 2.75 percent, respectively, of the market. The Megane is expected to do better next year with the popularity of the latest version, the Scenic, and new versions set to be rolled out, he said.
Sales of the new Espace minivan have exceeded company targets, and the sales mix is also better than expected, with 46 percent of sales in the more expensive RX2 version, he said.
Elsewhere, the group increased sales in central Europe.
In the region comprising Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and Poland, its car sales jumped 48 percent to 50,292, and its market share rose in each of the five countries.

Faure said the group aimed to increase its activities further east and hoped to start a small production operation in Russia with a partner in 1997. "Being among the first there would have its advantages," he said.
In Turkey, Renault displaced Fiat to become the top seller since the month of October. Its market share in Turkey was 29 percent in 1996.
Renault said sales in Brazil fell to 8,883 vehicles last year from 10,541 in 1995 because of higher import taxes.
It did not break out the rest of its Latin American sales but said in its statement that it "consolidated its positions".
